references.text: God's promise to Abraham to give his descendants the land from the River of Egypt to the Euphrates, including the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites - the same peoples mentioned in Exodus 3:17.
Parallel text in the same chapter where God says he will lead the Israelites out of Egypt to a land flowing with milk and honey, mentioning the same groups of people.
The promise to bring the people into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey.

God repeats the promise to lead the people to the land he swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, a land flowing with milk and honey, where Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites live.
The spies confirm that the land truly flows with milk and honey, as God had promised.
Moses reminds the people of the seven nations that the Lord will drive out before them: the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
The description of how the Lord brought Israel to this place and gave them this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
A prayer that God will bless Israel and the land he gave them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
The fulfillment of the promise when Joshua led the people into the land flowing with milk and honey.
Nehemiah reminds of the covenant with Abraham and the promise to give the land to the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites.
Stephen quotes God's promise to Moses to lead the people out of Egypt, a direct reference to the event in Exodus.
Paul mentions in his speech that God destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave the land to Israel as an inheritance.
Prophetic confirmation that the exodus from Egypt was based on an oath concerning the promised land.
Develops the promise from a prophecy about the future into a foundation for national identity and separation.
Specifies the promise regarding the land by naming the nations that will be driven out to make room.
Clarifies the means (the angel) to fulfill the promise of driving out the nations living in the promised land.
Confirms the promise by specifying that God's angel will lead the entry and destroy the mentioned nations.
Creates a theological contrast by showing that the promise of the land can be denied fulfillment due to disobedience.
Represents the original prophetic precursor (God's oath to Abraham) which Moses later confirms.
